content: Terbinafine is a medication specifically prescribed to treat fungal infections affecting the toenails and fingernails. It belongs to a class of drugs known as antifungals, and it works by inhibiting the growth of fungi. Terbinafine is available in tablet form and is taken orally. For fungal infections of the fingernails, it is typically taken once daily for six weeks. For toenail infections, it is usually taken once daily for 12 weeks. It is essential to follow the instructions on your prescription label carefully. If you have any questions or concerns, consult your doctor or pharmacist for clarification. Take terbinafine exactly as prescribed, without altering the dose or frequency. It is important to note that the fungal infection may not appear fully resolved until several months after completing the treatment, as it takes time for a healthy nail to grow back. In some cases, terbinafine may be prescribed for conditions other than nail fungal infections. If you have questions about alternative uses, consult your doctor or pharmacist for more information. Before starting terbinafine, inform your doctor and pharmacist if you are allergic to terbinafine or any other medications. Provide a complete list of all prescription and nonprescription medications, vitamins, supplements, and herbal products you are currently taking.g., warfarin), antidepressants (e.g., amitriptyline, nortriptyline), beta-blockers (e.g., atenolol, propranolol), cimetidine, immunosuppressants (e.g., cyclosporine, methotrexate), rifampin, and selegiline. Your doctor may need to adjust the dosages of your medications or monitor you closely for potential side effects. Additionally, inform your doctor if you have a history of kidney or liver disease, HIV, or AIDS. If you are pregnant, planning to become pregnant, or breastfeeding, notify your doctor. Terbinafine should not be taken while breastfeeding, and if you become pregnant during treatment, contact your doctor immediately. Unless otherwise directed by your doctor, you can continue your normal diet while taking terbinafine. If you miss a dose, take it as soon as you remember. However, if it is close to the time for your next scheduled dose, skip the missed dose and resume your regular dosing schedule. Do not take a double dose to compensate for a missed one. Terbinafine may cause side effects. Mild side effects include diarrhea, upset stomach, stomach pain, rash, itching, hives, and changes in or loss of taste. If these symptoms persist or worsen, inform your doctor. Severe side effects, though rare, require immediate medical attention. These include persistent upset stomach, loss of appetite, extreme fatigue, vomiting, pain in the upper right abdomen, dark urine, pale stools, severe or worsening skin rash, fever, sore throat, or other signs of infection. If you experience any unusual or serious side effects, contact your doctor promptly. Serious side effects can also be reported to the FDA's MedWatch Adverse Event Reporting program. Store terbinafine in its original container, tightly sealed, and out of reach of children. Keep it at room temperature, away from excessive heat and moisture, and do not store it in the bathroom. Dispose of expired or unused medication properly by consulting your pharmacist. In the event of an overdose, contact your local poison control center at 1-800-222-1222. If the individual has collapsed or is not breathing, call emergency services at 911. Keep all scheduled appointments with your doctor and laboratory, as certain tests may be required to monitor your response to terbinafine. Do not share this medication with others, and consult your pharmacist if you have questions about refilling your prescription. Terbinafine is sold under the brand names Lamisil® and Lamisil® AT.
